rationale: The detection patterns live in data, not in the prober's source, because a prober whose own module contained the literals it hunts for would report itself and force a self-exemption. Data rules keep the prober scannable by its own gate.
excluded_relative_dirs_note: Exclusion applies only to directory discovery. A file named explicitly on the command line is always scanned, which is how the planted fixtures are proved to be detected rather than merely skipped.

ABS_PATH_LITERAL.description: Absolute filesystem path baked into a string literal; breaks on any host whose layout differs.

TEMP_PATH_LITERAL.description: Hard-coded system temporary directory; makes the run depend on state outside the committed tree.

HOME_PATH_LITERAL.description: Tilde-relative path; resolves against the invoking user's home directory.

HOME_API.description: Call that resolves the user's home directory.

ENV_READ.description: Ambient environment read; the value is not in the committed tree, so the run is not reproducible from source alone.

NETWORK_IMPORT.description: Import of a network transport module; the suite must pass with outbound network disabled.

NETWORK_CALL.description: Call that opens an outbound connection.

SYS_PATH_MUTATION.description: Mutation of the import path with a value not anchored to __file__; hides a dependency on a directory layout that a clean clone may not have.
SYS_PATH_MUTATION.anchored_argument_note: An import path derived from __file__ names a directory inside the clone, so a clean clone always has it. That is not a portability defect. See literal_roles.sys_path_verdict.

SYS_PATH_ANCHORED.description: Import path extended with a __file__-anchored directory. Portable, but sys.path is process-global, so a position-0 insert can shadow the standard library and can change import resolution for every later test in the same discover run.
SYS_PATH_ANCHORED.preferred_alternative: importlib.util.spec_from_file_location, which imports a sibling module under -I without touching process-global state

literal_roles.rationale: A string literal is a portability defect only when the program uses it as a path. A literal that is compared against, asserted on, matched as a pattern or carried as data is a string under test, and reporting it trains reviewers to ignore the gate. Roles are decided from syntax, never from a list of forgiven values: a value allowlist would grow without bound and would forgive real defects that happened to share a spelling.
literal_roles.sys_path_verdict: sys.path.insert is an accepted pattern in this repository, not a portability defect. There is no installable package and no pyproject, tests run under python3 -I which implies -P, and so a test cannot import a module beside it by any other means except importlib.util.spec_from_file_location. Every mutation in the tree derives its argument from __file__, which always exists in a clean clone. The rule therefore fires only on an unanchored argument, and anchored mutations are reported as the advisory class SYS_PATH_ANCHORED for the process-global hazard they do carry.
literal_roles.string_operation_methods_note: str.join is deliberately absent. Its literal is the separator on the receiver, not an argument, so listing it would silently forgive os.path.join("/anchor", x) -- a real path construction that merely shares the method name.
literal_roles.filesystem_sinks_note_on_expanduser: expanduser touches nothing either, but it is the operation that turns a ~ literal into a host-specific path. Resolution is the use, so it counts.
literal_roles.filesystem_sinks_note: os.path.join, os.path.normpath, os.path.dirname and their kin are deliberately absent, and so is the Path constructor. They compute on strings and touch nothing, so a literal passed to them has not yet become a path in use. What makes Path(x) a use is the method called on it, which is why path_io_methods taints the receiver rather than the argument.
literal_roles.path_io_methods_note: Matched on the method name alone and taints the receiver expression, because Path(SCRATCH).mkdir() names no importable symbol a dotted-path table could match.

roles.COMPARISON_OPERAND: Argument to a string search or split method, or an operand of ==, !=, in or not in. The literal is a pattern being matched, not a location being opened.
roles.ASSERTION_OPERAND: Inside an assert statement or a unittest assertion call. The literal is the expected value of the thing under test.
roles.REGEX_PATTERN: Argument to a regular-expression or fnmatch function. The literal is a pattern.
roles.DIFF_PAYLOAD: The literal is itself a unified diff. A patch that quotes a defective line in order to remove it is the cure, not the disease.
roles.JSON_POINTER: The literal is the path member of an RFC 6902 JSON Patch operation. A JSON Pointer addresses a document, not a filesystem.
roles.FSTRING_FRAGMENT: The literal is a piece of an f-string preceded by an interpolation, so it cannot be an absolute path however it begins.
roles.PATTERN_TABLE: The literal is an element of a module-level collection whose every use in that module is a comparison. A detector's own table of forbidden prefixes is data, not usage.
roles.TEST_FIXTURE: The literal appears in a test function that makes assertions, and reaches no filesystem sink. It is a value under test. A test that does open("/tmp/x") still fires, because that literal does reach a sink.
